goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: align-items mixin emits invalid value for legacy box model: -webkit-box-align/-moz-box-align should use 'middle' instead of 'center', making vendor prefix fallbacks no-op on old engines (mixins.scss:105-110)

adjudication.rationale: In mixins.scss the align-items mixin sets `-webkit-box-align: $alignment;` (no `-moz-box-align` is emitted at all), and legacy `box-align` accepts `center` as a valid value in old flexbox implementations—there’s no evidence in the diff that `center` is invalid or must be `middle`. The finding also cites `-moz-box-align`, which is not present in the mixin, indicating a misread of the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: order(2)/order(3) applied to .extra-info-wrapper and .panel while siblings stay at default order:0 can invert intended visual order relative to DOM position (topic.scss:29-30, header.scss:38-42)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` and `@include order(3)` on `.panel`, but the finding’s claim that this "can invert intended visual order" is speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone. In `header.scss`, `.contents` is made a flex container, so `order(3)` will affect `.panel`, but we can’t see sibling markup/orders to judge intent. In `topic.scss`, no parent flex container is shown in the diff, so `order(2)` may have no effect at all. Thus the asserted problem isn’t concretely demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Vertical centering in .small-action via align-items:center and removed desc padding/margin changes multi-line content layout, collapsing paragraph spacing between adjacent p elements (topic-post.scss:263-265)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce the described layout changes in `.small-action`: it becomes a flex container with `@include align-items(center);` (topic-post.scss) and `.small-action-desc` loses its previous top/bottom padding and `margin-top`, while nested `p` elements change from `margin: 5px 0;` to `margin: 0;`, and `> p` loses `padding-top: 4px;`. This will indeed remove vertical spacing between adjacent paragraphs and can affect multi-line alignment. However, whether this is a *defect* (vs. an intentional visual adjustment) cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: -moz-inline-box in inline-flex() is a nonexistent/removed property, indicating the legacy Firefox fallback path was never functional (mixins.scss:100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `inline-flex()` mixin that includes `display: -moz-inline-box;` (mixins.scss). Whether `-moz-inline-box` is “nonexistent/removed” in Firefox, and whether this fallback “was never functional,” is a browser-support claim not verifiable from the diff itself. The diff only shows an extra (possibly obsolete) display value that would be ignored if unsupported, not a demonstrable defect in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mixins emit legacy box-model prefixes (-webkit-box, -ms-flexbox, box-ordinal-group) with semantics differing from modern flexbox; e.g., align-items(center) is invalid for -webkit-box-align in some legacy implementations (P3, rendering-compatibility concern)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new flexbox mixins in `mixins.scss` that emit legacy flexbox/box syntax (`display: -webkit-box`, `-ms-flexbox`, `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, etc.) and then uses them in multiple places (`@include flexbox()`, `@include align-items(center)`, `@include order(3)`). These legacy properties can have different value expectations/semantics than modern flexbox (notably `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` is historically 1-based vs `order` being 0-based), which can lead to inconsistent rendering on older engines. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove a concrete break in supported targets, so it’s best treated as a rendering-compatibility concern rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: header.scss `.panel` with order(3) in unwrapped flex container may squish/overflow on narrow viewports since old float layout wrapped but flex row does not (flex-wrap: nowrap default, no flex-shrink guard)

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` was changed from a float-based layout (`.title { float: left; }` and `.panel { float: right; }`) to a flex container via `@include flexbox()` with centering. `.panel` now uses `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)`. The diff does not add any `flex-wrap` (defaults to `nowrap`) or sizing constraints (e.g., `flex-shrink: 0` / `min-width`) for the flex children, so on narrow viewports the flex row could compress items or overflow depending on content. This is a concrete, diff-grounded responsiveness/layout risk, but the diff alone can’t prove it will definitely break in practice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: order(3)/order(2) declarations are silent-pass traps: no effect if the parent isn't actually the flexified .contents container, so reordering may silently do nothing; also extra-info-wrapper with order(2) may reorder before panel in templates that render it after

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `@include order(3)` on `.panel` (header.scss) and `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` (topic.scss). The `order` property only has effect when the element is a flex item (i.e., its parent is `display:flex/inline-flex`). While `.contents` is made a flex container in this diff, the diff does not show that `.panel` is actually a direct child of `.contents` in the DOM, nor does it show any flex parent for `.extra-info-wrapper`. So these `order(...)` additions can become silent no-ops depending on markup/context, which is a concrete maintainability/robustness concern; the template-ordering claim is speculative from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy-prefixed mixins emit invalid/ineffective declarations: -webkit-box-align: baseline unsupported in 2009 spec, and -moz/-webkit-box-ordinal-group semantics differ from modern order, potentially causing wrong alignment in older browsers

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new flexbox helper mixins in `mixins.scss` and starts using `@include order(2/3)` and `@include align-items(baseline)` in several stylesheets. The `order($val)` mixin maps modern `order` directly to legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but those legacy properties are 1-based and have different semantics than modern `order` (0-based), so using the same numeric value can yield different ordering in older prefixed implementations. Similarly, `align-items($alignment)` emits multiple legacy properties (including `-webkit-box-align`) whose accepted values/behavior can differ from modern `align-items`, so the compatibility intent may be undermined. This is a concrete, diff-grounded concern about legacy-browser behavior, but it’s not verifiable from the diff alone that it causes a real defect in the app’s supported browser set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `.small-action` flexification removes avatar/desc spacing contract: fixed 4em/0.5em padding replaced by flex item width, so absent/hidden avatar causes text to collapse flush against container edge; flex default min-width:auto can also cause overflow of long unbroken content

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `.small-action` to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and replaces `.small-action-desc`’s previous fixed left offset (`padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;` plus `margin-top: 5px;`) with `padding: 0 1.5%`. That is a concrete layout/spacing contract change tied to the avatar’s former reserved space. However, the finding’s specific claims about an “absent/hidden avatar” scenario and flex `min-width:auto` overflow are not directly verifiable from the diff alone (no evidence here that the avatar can be conditionally absent/hidden, nor any content constraints shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of .bullet margin-top: 5px compensation: flex centering centers boxes not text baselines, and extra-info-wrapper line-height: 1.5 vs unchanged title line-height may cause visible baseline misalignment between bullet row and title

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `.badge-wrapper &.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` in `topic.scss`, but it also updates the `.bullet` styling in `badges.css.scss` to use `@include inline-flex()` with `@include align-items(baseline)`, not flex centering. The claim that “flex centering centers boxes not text baselines” does not match the `.bullet` change shown. The additional concern about `extra-info-wrapper { line-height: 1.5; }` causing baseline misalignment with an “unchanged title line-height” can’t be verified from this diff because no title line-height is shown here, making the stated visible misalignment speculative.
